November 9, 2000
Legalization of Pot Doesn't Generate Much Smoke
(MarijuanaNews note: The usual pun in the headline conditions the readers not to take the subject too seriously. It also tells the readers that marijuana legalization is a fringe issue. In fact, only a relatively small shift in opinions would put us in the majority. One of the problems with a survey like this is that in some parts of the country people are still afraid to give their honest opinion.)

Utica, N.Y. (Reuters/Zogby) –

Most Americans think that marijuana should remain illegal, according to a recent poll.

In the Zogby America survey of 1,028 adults nationwide, roughly two-thirds of those responding (66.5%) did not think that marijuana should be legalized.

A dissenting 28.7% felt that the drug should be legalized, and 4.8% were not sure.

This poll has a margin of error of +/-3.2%.

Younger respondents were more likely to favor legalization; 39.8% of those aged 18-29 felt it would be a positive step, compared to 30.1% of those 30-49, 28.7% of individuals 50-64, and only 21.7% of those over 65.

Residents of America's large cities were more likely to support legalization of marijuana than were those living in smaller cities, suburbs, or rural locales.

Whites and African Americans were equally supportive of retaining the ban on marijuana, as were men and women. See
NORML Study Reveals Blacks Arrested For Marijuana At More Than Twice The Rate For Whites

What we asked:

" Do you agree or disagree that marijuana should be legalized?''

(MarijuanaNews note: The " L " word gets the most resistance. If the question had been, " should marijuana be taken out of the black market and taxed and regulated? " the results would hav e been more positive. Nonetheless, this is all the more interesting following the Alaska initiative, which went far beyond simple " legalization " and got almost 40%. Alaska may be more " libertarian " than most, but when an active campaign is waged, we do better.)
